findings.title: unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser row exists
findings.body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can legitimately return `nil` (a logged-in user who has never visited/been emailed about the topic, or whose topic_users row was removed), and the next line immediately calls `tu.notification_level`, raising `NoMethodError` and returning a 500 to a user who just clicked a link in an email. The action should create the record (e.g. via `TopicUser.change`) or bail out gracefully when the row is missing.

findings.title: Writing notification_level directly instead of TopicUser.change leaves stale metadata and lets the mute be auto-reverted
findings.body: The action assigns `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!`, bypassing `TopicUser.change`. Consequences: (1) `notifications_reason_id` and `notifications_changed_at` are not set, so the row still looks like an auto-assigned level. `TopicUser.update_last_read` re-promotes a topic to `tracking` precisely when `notifications_reason_id IS NULL` and the view-time threshold is exceeded, so the user's unsubscribe can be silently undone the next time they read the topic. (2) No `MessageBus.publish("/topic/<id>", notification_level_change: ...)` is sent, so other open clients/tabs keep showing the old notification level. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: level)` instead.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe exposed over GET (CSRF-able)
findings.body: `unsubscribe` is routed as a GET (see config/routes.rb) and mutates the user's notification level. Rails' CSRF token verification only applies to non-GET verbs, and `check_xhr` is explicitly skipped for this action, so any third-party page can mute arbitrary topics for a logged-in Discourse user simply by embedding ``. Browser/extension link prefetching can also trigger it unintentionally. Either make the mutation happen on a POST/PUT from a confirmation page, or require a signed, single-use unsubscribe key in the URL.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, breaking callers that don't pass it
findings.body: `unsubscribe_link` gained a `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation, but `Email::MessageBuilder#body`/`#html_part` render it for every caller that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. Any mailer (core or plugin) that sets `add_unsubscribe_link` without also supplying `unsubscribe_url` will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and fail to send the email — the spec change in this PR (adding `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` so the existing test keeps passing) demonstrates exactly this breakage. Add a default for `unsubscribe_url` in `MessageBuilder#initialize` or only append the per-topic sentence when the option is present.

findings.title: Unsubscribe confirmation text is wrong for watching/tracking topics
findings.body: The server action downgrades `watching`/`tracking` to `regular` on the first visit and only sets `muted` when the level is already `regular` or lower, yet the page unconditionally says "You will stop receiving notifications for <topic>" (and the email says "To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here"). A user who was watching a topic will still receive notifications for replies/mentions after following the link, so the message is factually wrong and the user has to click twice. Either mute unconditionally or make the text reflect the resulting notification level.

findings.title: Unsubscribe link does not work for recipients without an active session
findings.body: `:unsubscribe` is added to the `ensure_logged_in` filter, so a recipient who clicks the unsubscribe link in an email from a browser where they are not signed in gets a `Discourse::NotLoggedIn` (silent redirect to the homepage for HTML requests) and nothing is unsubscribed, with no explanation. Email unsubscribe links are routinely opened in a context without a session; the flow needs a signed per-user token in the URL (like the digest `DigestUnsubscribeKey`) rather than relying on the session cookie.

findings.title: No specs for the new unsubscribe endpoint
findings.body: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action changes persisted user state and is reachable from every notification email, but no request/controller spec was added. Uncovered behaviours that are currently broken or risky: missing `TopicUser` row, the watching→regular vs regular→muted transition, the slug-mismatch 301 redirect, anonymous access, and the JSON vs HTML response paths. Only `spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb` was touched.

findings.title: Template path likely not resolvable for the topicUnsubscribe route
findings.body: The route is registered as `topicUnsubscribe` and its controller/view are named `topic-unsubscribe`, which the Discourse resolver looks up as `topicUnsubscribe` / `topic_unsubscribe` / `topic-unsubscribe`. This template is registered under the key `topic/unsubscribe` (because of its directory), which does not match any of those forms, so the route may render an empty outlet. Either move the file to `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs` or set `renderTemplate`/`templateName` explicitly.

findings.title: Setting the computed notificationReasonText has no effect
findings.body: `topic.set("details.notificationReasonText", null)` targets `notificationReasonText`, which is a computed property on the topic-details model (derived from `notification_level`/`notifications_reason_id`) with no setter. Assigning to it will not clear the displayed text (in Ember 1.x the getter is re-invoked and its return value cached; in later Ember versions it throws), so the stated intent of hiding the notification reason is not achieved. Use a flag that the component/template checks instead.
